If you could go back to the early days of the internet, would you handle your privacy differently? Most of us would. We would be more selective about the services we use and more careful about what we share. Since time machines don't exist, we have to face the reality of the present. Your personal data is being sold publicly right now.

Right now, your phone number, email address, home address, and even your family relationships are being packaged and resold to marketers, insurance companies, and hackers. While privacy protection features built into Safari and Mail can block some tracking when you browse the web, they cannot retroactively erase the data that has been collected over the years and spread across hundreds of broker databases. Data brokers have built a multi-billion dollar industry dedicated to collecting your digital data, packaging it into products, and selling it. It is time to remove your personal information from the market and the internet. Let's look at how.

The security risks of the data broker industry

However, the danger goes far beyond annoying spam calls. When your data is spread everywhere, you become an easy target for sophisticated cyberattacks. Since the industry is largely unregulated, your most private information—including past employment, residential addresses, and previous loan records—can be easily purchased. This poses a tremendous security concern.

Modern scammers use data provided by brokers to carry out highly personalised (and hard-to-detect) phishing attacks. When scammers already know your job title, where you have lived, or the names of your colleagues and friends, they can easily bypass your instinctive defences. If a scammer knows you inside and out, they only need to strike when you let your guard down, and the chances of success are extremely high.

For those concerned about personal safety, these websites and brokers provide stalkers with a publicly searchable database. By mapping out your relationships with relatives and neighbours, brokers offer a ready-made location blueprint for those who deliberately keep a low profile and wish to remain out of the spotlight.

The solution: automatic data removal with Incogni

This ecosystem is shockingly large—indeed, daunting. Trying to request the deletion of your data from hundreds of websites one by one is essentially a full-time job, and the success rate is nearly zero, because if it were easy to do, these brokers couldn't stay in business. What you need is a solution that understands how this industry operates and can help you reclaim your right to privacy.

This is precisely why a service like Incogni becomes essential to your life—both in the digital world and the real one. It transforms a massive problem (your data being everywhere and sold at will) into a solved one, offering a one-stop solution. Instead of you spending months tracking down data brokers one by one, Incogni automatically handles the tedious, repetitive back-and-forth of opt-out requests on your behalf. They ensure your data isn't just deleted once, but that they continuously prevent brokers from re-scraping and re-adding your information.

Incogni's comprehensive dashboard lets you track the progress of your personal data removal in real time, including:

  • The number of databases that may contain your information
  • Removal requests being sent on your behalf
  • Completed removals and ongoing follow-up remediation work

The real benefits of data removal for the privacy-conscious

Once you are removed from internet broker databases, you and your family will see results immediately

  • When companies can't buy your number, scam calls and spam texts go down.
  • Scammers lose their target. Identity thieves often obtain victim information from broker websites.
  • Your home address stays private, making it harder for stalkers and harassers to find your residence.
  • Your credit score stays healthy, as reduced data exposure lowers the risk of identity theft and strengthens your overall financial wellbeing.
